text:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] us-east-1a - elevated error rates and token latency for inference-pool-us-east-1a detected. Auto-threshold triggered at 2156789012. Paging @alice (oncall-ml) and @jamie (sre). Severity: S2.

alice (oncall-ml): I’m on it. Quick ask: is this latency only for generation endpoints, or embeddings too?

jamie (sre): seeing 502/504 spikes from inference frontends -> backend connection resets. Embeddings less affected but some token latency increase. I’m pulling ELB/NLB health.

lee (eng-runtime): KV cache miss rate jumped ~8x. Affected requests are mainly hitting g5 instances in us-east-1a. Could be packet loss to those AZ hosts.

sam (networking): running quick check against AZ network plane. traceroute from edge -> us-east-1a hop 6 shows intermittent * * *. Packet loss at hop 6/7. Looks like provider fiber flap, not instance CPU.

jamie (sre): ELB health checks failing intermittently for target group inference-us-east-1a-tg. NLB shows high target connection errors.

alice (oncall-ml): customer impact? any ongoing pageable user requests failing?

kyle (support): CS queue: a handful of customers reporting generation timeouts, one large customer (acct: streamlytics) hitting 5–10% error rate on critical path. They're on Dedicated in us-east-1a.

maria (product-ops): activating cross-zone fallback policy in the Console now? We should prefer routing to us-east-1b until this stabilizes.

lee (eng-runtime): plan: enable routing policy to prefer healthy regions and gradually drain us-east-1a. Steps: 1) set smart-routing preference to prefer_us-east-1b for profile inference-default. 2) scale up spare capacity in us-east-1b pool by +20%. 3) reduce DNS TTL for inference.redwoodapis.com to 30s.

jamie (sre): doing quick verification of ENI and instance metrics:
```
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-1a" --query '[].{Id:NetworkInterfaceId,Status:Status,TxErrors:Attachment}'
```
response indicates a subset of ENIs showing TxErrors spike > 1000.

sam (networking): confirmed with cloud provider status page — they report a fiber maintenance causing increased packet loss in us-east-1a affecting some AZ internal paths. They have an ongoing ticket.

alice (oncall-ml): immediate mitigation: switch live traffic away from the impacted AZ using edge routing and target group weights. Jamie — can you shift 75% of traffic to us-east-1b now and leave 25% to test? Keep short TTLs.

jamie (sre): doing it now. Command:
```
# lower TTL
kubectl exec -n control-plane deploy/dns-controller -- sh -c "update-ttl inference.redwoodapis.com 30"
# adjust weights in our routing plane
redwoodctl routing set-weight --route inference-default --region us-east-1b --weight 75
redwoodctl routing set-weight --route inference-default --region us-east-1a --weight 25
```

jamie (sre): applied weight change, scaling us-east-1b pool +30% (warm spare). Monitoring.

lee (eng-runtime): KV cache warmup in 1b starting, but expect slight initial latency as caches populate. Will enable aggressive prefix caching for hot prompts.

ana (cust-success): pinging streamlytics to let them know we're mitigating and routing traffic away from their Dedicated seats in us-east-1a.

kyle (support): sending template: "We're aware of elevated timeouts originating from us-east-1a. We're routing traffic to us-east-1b and will update when resolved."

maria (product-ops): 👍 reduce TTL to 15s if routing needs faster convergence. Keep customers updated.

jamie (sre): after weight change: error rate down 60% overall for inference endpoints. us-east-1a still showing sporadic connection resets for direct sessions. Some stateful sessions will still hit those nodes — we should advise customers with pinned dedicated capacity.

alice (oncall-ml): action items while mitigating:
- keep public status updated (maria)
- reach out to any Dedicated customers pinned to us-east-1a (ana/kyle)
- open provider escalation (sam)
- prepare failback plan when provider confirms stable (jamie/lee)

sam (networking): provider escalated to network ops, they estimate 30–60 min for stabilization depending on rehome of fiber. They recommend our routing changes.

lee (eng-runtime): for Dedicated customers: we can offer live migration to warm spare hosts in 1b if they accept brief rekeying. Need product sign-off. @maria

maria (product-ops): ok to offer migration to affected customers as manual assist. Prioritize customers with SLOs.

ana (cust-success): Streamlytics confirmed they see fewer errors after our routing change. They want ETA to fully restore. I'll keep them posted.

jamie (sre): monitoring graphs: latency P95 dropped from 2.1s -> 0.9s after routing shift. Error rate for streamlytics down to 1.2% (was 8%).

alice (oncall-ml): good. I'll remain on pager for the next 45m, then hand off to @jamie for follow-up. If provider says stable and error rates hold for 20m, we'll start gradual failback.

incident-bot: escalation reminder in 30m.

jamie (sre): running tcpdump on a sample host in us-east-1a to capture resets:
```
# sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst) != 0' -c 200 > /tmp/rst-capture.log
```
collected resets show bursty pattern synced with provider maintenance window.

sam (networking): provider sent updated note: "we've finished a fiber swap, monitoring for convergence. Some residual packet loss expected for next 5–15 minutes."

lee (eng-runtime): rolling health-check threshold back to normal for us-east-1a only after 20m stable metrics. Plan for failback: revert routing weights to 50/50, then 100% over 15 minutes while watching KV miss and error rates.

jamie (sre): preparing handoff notes for follow-up:
- current status: routing to 1b (75%), errors down 60%
- provider reports fiber swap completed
- still monitoring ENI TxErrors in 1a
- recommended wait: 20m stable before revert

jamie (sre): handing off to @jamie (sre) for next shift at 2156789312. (I'll stay reachable.)

alice (oncall-ml): thanks team. Final ask before handoff: add incident label and create postmortem ticket with initial timeline + customer impact.

maria (product-ops): creating incident ticket in tracker now and will post to status page.

ana (cust-success): will compile affected customers list for outreach.

kyle (support): closing customer-facing message draft. Will send update in 10m.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] 15m after mitigation: overall error rate stabilized ~1.1%. Continue monitoring.

jamie (sre): agreed, leaving monitoring checks in place. Marking runbook item: add explicit provider-fiber-flap play with step-by-step routing controls.

alice (oncall-ml): handing on-call to jamie now. If anything flares, page immediately.

(THREAD NOTE: root message at 2156789012, handoff complete at 2156789312)
